Significance Note: Birthplace of Siddhartha Gautama (the Buddha); UNESCO World Heritage Site.
Where the Buddha attained enlightenment beneath the Bodhi Tree.
Where the Buddha delivered his first sermon and set the wheel of Dharma in motion.
Where the Buddha attained parinirvana (final passing).
Major teaching site near Nalanda where the Buddha delivered the Lotus Sutra and other key sermons.
First pilgrimage destination in Christian history; venerated as the site of Jesus's crucifixion and resurrection.
Spiritual center of the Roman Catholic Church and traditional burial site of Saint Peter; one of the "three great pilgrimages of Christendom" historically named by Pope Alexander VI.
Endpoint of the Way of St. James; one of the "three great pilgrimages of Christendom"; traditional burial site of Saint James the Greater.

Site: Sanctuary of Our Lady of Lourdes
Significance Note: Major Roman Catholic Marian pilgrimage site associated with the 1858 apparitions to Bernadette Soubirous.
Most frequently visited Catholic shrine in Poland; home to the Black Madonna of Częstochowa icon.
Birthplace of Rama; site of the Ram Janmabhoomi temple.
Birthplace of Krishna; major Vaishnava pilgrimage center.
Where the Ganges enters the plains; one of the four sites of the Kumbh Mela.
Spiritual capital of Hinduism on the banks of the Ganges; home to the Kashi Vishwanath Jyotirlinga; the Sapta Puri article describes Varanasi as the "most holy" of the seven sacred cities.
Major South Indian temple city sacred to both Shaiva and Vaishnava traditions; home to the Kamakshi Amman Temple.
The most significant mosque in Islam; encloses the Kaaba and is the focal point of the annual Hajj pilgrimage.
The second largest mosque and second holiest site in Islam after Masjid al-Haram; contains Muhammad's tomb beneath the Green Dome.
The third holiest site in Islam after Mecca and Medina; on the Haram al-Sharif / Temple Mount where Muhammad is believed to have ascended to heaven during the Night Journey.

Sacred burial site revered by Judaism Christianity and Islam; per the article some sources rank the mosque as the 4th holiest in Islam (other sources rank other sites 4th); traditional burial site of Abraham.
The fourth holiest Islamic site for Shia Muslims and the burial site of Ali ibn Abi Talib whom Shias revere as the first Imam.
